doors.label: Tax cap
doors.sentence: "Keep property taxes at reasonable rates, while managing inflation." No cap, no formula, no number, no supermajority rule. Term record: 3.2% (2023), 7.93% (2024), 8.68% (2025), 7.28% overall / 9.34% residential (2026). His site claims the term kept increases "in the bottom half of regional municipalities."

doors.label: Downtown order
doors.sentence: "Work with VicPD, Bylaw, the Province, and service providers to limit and restrict open drug consumption and to reduce street disorder." No Public Order Team, no unified command, no 6am–10pm bylaw hours, no staffing number.

doors.label: Housing
doors.sentence: "Make Victoria attractive to families - develop and expand the Family Housing Regulation (requiring multi-bedroom homes in new builds)." A composition instrument. No unit total, no 25/20/15/30 mix, no quarterly composition reporting.

doors.label: Written program
doors.sentence: Authorized 2026 site with a 10-section platform (~70 commitments), a 10-section Achievements record, a stated objective, endorsements and videos. Not costed, no dates, no service standards, no numbers except canopy 40% and CRHC 3,000–3,500.

cells.quote: Make Victoria attractive to families - develop and expand the Family Housing Regulation (requiring multi-bedroom homes in new builds).
cells.why: Commits + comparable: a bedroom-mix regulation is a composition lever, adopted June 2024 (tiered — 30% at 3+ bedrooms in buildings ≤3 storeys; 10% at 3+ plus 20% at 2+ above). Not M6's instrument: no total target, no 25/20/15/30 mix, no quarterly composition reporting, no scored land disposition. "over 9,000 new homes approved" is a campaign approvals claim — not occupancy, not stamped as an ACTW figure.

cells.quote: Expand by 3,000 - 3,500 the number of affordable homes built by the Capital Regional Housing Corporation.
cells.why: Commits with a number, but through a regional build vehicle, not a land instrument: no public inventory of city-owned land, no acquisition fund, no scored disposition, no right-of-first-refusal, no co-ops. Co-ops appear only on the 2022 legacy site. CRHC vice-chair is a seat held, not a source.

cells.quote: Get more homes built faster - streamline development processes to reduce costs and build-times.
cells.why: Commits, no instrument: no published service standard by permit type, no 6-week / 6-month / 9-month targets, no one-stop centre, no tenure priority queue, no AI pre-screening, no variance report. No permit benchmark published in four years — absence is Record, not Opposed.

cells.quote: Approve market and non-market housing proposals aligned with the Official Community Plan.
cells.why: Commits + comparable, on the pre-zoned by-right pipeline M8 names. Supporting action: named YES on Missing Middle 26 Jan 2023 (6–3) and on the 28 Sep 2023 overhaul (7–2) — "I think it is justified to make some pretty drastic changes to this policy." No 5% vacancy target, no DCC reduction for purpose-built rental, no suite amnesty. Cluster = 1 of 55.

cells.quote: Work with VicPD, Bylaw, the Province, and service providers to limit and restrict open drug consumption and to reduce street disorder.
cells.why: Commits + comparable: the same multi-agency composition DPOT names. Context, not a second mark: campaign claims a "community safety field hub on Pandora for police and bylaw" and "shared enforcement priorities" with the new Chief. Absent: unified command, single field supervisor per shift, 8am briefing, weekly DPOT dashboard.

cells.quote: Work collaboratively with VicPD to address criminal element that embeds itself in unhoused community.
cells.why: Commits to concentrating on disorder drivers; no instrument — no hotspot data, no published aggregate locations, no Crown-counsel coordination, no focused-deterrence model. The data is what this measure is.

cells.quote: Continue to work towards winding down sheltering in Victoria's parks.
cells.why: Commits + same instrument: M33 adds no rules and no staff, it is consistent enforcement of the sheltering bylaws already on the books. Supporting action: voted YES 18 Jul 2024, 8–1, on directing staff to cost the enforcement needed to compel shelters down by designated times. Context, not a second mark: "This will not somehow solve homelessness."

cells.what: drug-use buffer (City: list + bylaw/DPOT + VicPD/CDSA; not City seizure)

cells.quote: Hired the City's first-ever Parks Relocation Coordinator, who successfully housed over 70 people formerly sheltering in parks"; "Wound down the practice of overnight sheltering in parks, followed by soil remediation and several playground installations.
cells.why: Capacity-first in practice. No 2026 promise here, and nothing contradicted — shown, not scored, not in n. Absent: same-day removal protocol, 5pm capacity board, named reclaimed spaces with patrol hours, all-night lighting.

cells.what: tax glide path (capped on the residential rate)
cells.quote: Keep property taxes at reasonable rates, while managing inflation.
cells.why: Agrees + neither: names the goal, no cap, no formula, no number, no supermajority override. Record beside it, in his own campaign words: the term kept increases "in the bottom half of regional municipalities" — 3.2 / 7.93 / 8.68 / 7.28, and 9.34% residential in 2026, roughly 35% cumulative. FLAG: he is not named in the 7 May 2026 adoption (6–3; only Gardiner, Kim and Hammond named opposed) and eScribe returns 403, so his individual YES is inference, not a source. If the recorded vote is obtained and he is named, this cell becomes Opposed −1.0.

cells.quote: Recapitalized capital reserves for the first time in 30 years (i.e. began saving money again for infrastructure).
cells.why: Serves M66c's goal of not borrowing against the next council; it is also the sweep-into-reserves M66b is written against. No 2026 promise on either, nothing contradicted — shown, not scored. Absent: over-collection credit, 1.5% band, debt ceiling, quarterly debt metrics, non-balancing-item rule.

cells.quote: Advocate to senior governments to properly fund their services and reduce 'downloading' of costs to local governments.
cells.why: Commits + comparable: names downloading directly, and he has run the instrument — co-sponsor with Coun. Hammond of the 14 Nov 2024 Caledonia Place motion directing the Mayor to write to 12 CRD municipalities and 3 electoral areas to take on hosting it: "For too long, North Park has been expected to shoulder much of the obligations of sheltering and supportive housing for the entire region." Absent: quarterly ledger, twice-yearly UBCM/FCM cadence, published refusal threshold.

cells.what: CRD cost and the Goldstream plant
business, downtown, one mandate not a new office
cells.quote: Revitalize downtown by creating a new vision for a prosperous, fun, safe downtown, working with Downtown Victoria Business Association, the Chamber of Commerce, the South Island Prosperity Project, and diverse community partners.
cells.why: Commits, no instrument: no vacancy figure or target, no 5-day business licence standard, no 6-week tenant-improvement target, no simplification charter, no Strategic Economic Plan, no Conference Centre numbers. Context, and a divergence: "Help transform SIPP into a comprehensive economic development agency with stable regional funding" adds an agency where M73b says one mandate, not a new office.

cells.what: capital threshold, short-stay parking (15-min grace; first-hour gated Year 2), permit fees
Host Nations Foundation. Topic never drops out of the 12. A dash is still allowed on M1–M5.
cells.quote: Work collaboratively and respectfully with the Songhees and Xwsepsum Nations in government-to-government relations.
cells.why: Commits to the relationship and to named joint deliverables — "Work with local Nations to create a public memorial to Residential Schools survivors"; "Listen to and enable the Songhees and Xwsepsum in developing the Matullia lands in Rock Bay" — but none of the five instruments: no quarterly working table with published summaries, no 5% Indigenous procurement standard, no dual-naming programme, no cultural protocols, no urban Indigenous services liaison.

cells.what: tenant protections, STR, indoor heat (M9c struck; 26°C gated)
cells.quote: Strengthen protections for renters by reviewing and expanding the new Tenant Protection During Redevelopment Bylaw.
cells.why: Commits + same instrument, twice over. M9: the bylaw he is expanding is the demoviction-compensation instrument M9 names; the 30 Jul 2026 enhancement carried unanimously (5 months' rent at 5–9 years, to 24 months at 40+). M64 indoor heat: co-mover with Dell and Thompson of the 14 May 2026 cooling motion (unanimous, 26°C standard cited), and named again on 23 Jul 2026 when council directed bylaw amendments so landlords cannot prohibit cooling devices — M64's step 1 exactly. M9c is struck and is not scored. Absent: 12-month notice, replacement-unit ratio, Renters' Hub, STR licensing regime. Cluster = 1 of 55.

cells.quote: I'll continue working regionally to address homelessness, mental health, and addictions by building on the early successes of the Community Safety and Wellbeing Plan, which has reduced visible homelessness and invested in sheltering, housing, prevention, and recovery.
cells.why: Commits + comparable: a supportive-housing-with-partners package, and the campaign records working with BC Housing on a low-barrier Rock Bay shelter and funding a social service centre that housed over 100 people. Absent and material: no 50% target, Housing First not named, no STEP throughput, no Coordinated Access, no published outcome metric of any kind.

cells.what: childcare, doctors, youth (M13 school food is $0 → M13d)
cells.quote: Attract family doctors to the city by supporting a civic health hub on the Colwood model.
cells.why: Commits + comparable on M13b: city-enabled clinic space is the recruitment lever, without the s.224 permissive tax exemption, the fast-track clinic permitting or a published net-new-practitioners number. Context, not a second mark: free youth bus passes across the region (M13c-adjacent). Childcare is absent entirely — no spaces target, no 60-day permit, no pre-zoning.

cells.quote: Begin recycling programs in SD61 facilities and schools.
cells.why: Commits to a joint City–SD61 programme — the only SD61 line on the site — with none of the instrument: no standing agreement, no published annual work plan, no joint public meeting, no joint-use facilities agreement, no safe-routes-to-school programme, no single named City contact. Context: "Make it safer for kids to get around Victoria by foot, bike, and transit." M13 school food is $0 and is not scored.

cells.quote: Actions over words. 2026 promise: "Make downtown safer and cleaner - Advance and adapt the Community Safety and Wellbeing (CSWB) plan." Sourced action against it: voted NO 21 May 2026, 6–2 with Dell (Loughton absent), on exploring spray-paint sale restrictions — "I'm also not convinced that minors are the issue here — we've been presented with zero evidence that minors are in fact committing these vandalistic crimes"; "I'm unsure if using City staff's time on this endeavour was worth the cause.
cells.why: Agrees graffiti is a problem, opposes this instrument, offers no other. Absent: 48-hour removal standard, sanitation hours, pest plan, public-art replacement. The incumbent cap (max Partial+ 1.5) does not bind at 0.5.

cells.what: mobility + Vision Zero (M39 30 km/h struck; calming is M38)
cells.quote: Advance a light-rail feasibility study and business case for the proposed Reconciliation Corridor Initiative on the E&N line between Langford and Victoria.
cells.why: Commits + same instrument, twice: M22's E&N endorsement and station-area work, and M41's protected network — "Expand Victoria's AAA cycling network and better connect it to regional infrastructure" (campaign records 45 km built, incl. Blanshard, Gorge, Fort, Dallas). Absent: adaptive signals (M19), intersection redesign programme (M38), school-zone site list (M40), Vision Zero audit rule (M42), hood-height advocacy (M42b). M39 struck, not scored.

cells.what: walking and transit the City controls
cells.quote: Improve transit by advancing dedicated bus lanes and RapidBus in Victoria and regionally, and by creating regular, direct service to YYJ.
cells.why: Commits + comparable: bus lanes are the City-controlled transit lever M23b names, without naming it as an annual capital line. Context, not a second mark: "Make safer streets for pedestrians by adding more signalized crosswalks and improving sidewalks." Absent: sidewalk gap inventory, published crossing standard, 1.0 m/s signal timing, published transit position adopted in open session, published record of Commission decisions.

cells.quote: Created first-ever accessible playground in Victoria, at Stadacona Park"; "Added new dock, portable washrooms, and bike racks at Banfield Park.
cells.why: No 2026 promise on either subject and nothing contradicted — shown, not scored. Absent: 24-month accessibility audit, public dashboard, remediation capital line, curb-cut/tactile/audible programme, Disability Advisory Committee, and any downtown washroom network or 500 m spacing.

cells.quote: Invest in road paving, complete streets, bridges, sidewalks, cycling, and other public infrastructure.
cells.why: Commits + comparable, with a delivered number behind it: "Increased road paving from 1km to 10-15 km annually," plus Bay Street Bridge repair and water-main renewal. Absent: 7-day report-to-fix pothole standard, published condition-based prioritization, explicit maintenance-before-new sequencing rule.

cells.what: VicPD funding + regional review (convene-and-publish; no binding other force)
cells.quote: Work with surrounding jurisdictions and the Province to create a regional police force.
cells.why: Commits + comparable on M29b's file, going past the review to the outcome. The action behind it, same file: he moved the 3 Mar 2026 motion funding 2 rather than 4 new VicPD officers (seconded Loughton, carried 5–4; Coleman, Gardiner, Hammond and Alto opposed; the Police Board voted unanimously on 16 Jun 2026 to appeal) — "I think the two things can be true at the same time — that the VicPD needs more resources, and Victorians are already paying the most in the province for policing per capita… the current model is not working." Absent: Esquimalt funding formula, service-consumption metrics, time-boxed costed review, terms of reference, published offer and refusal.

cells.what: safety dashboard, published enforcement record, crime target

cells.quote: Protect Victoria's historic Old Town and heritage buildings.
cells.why: Commits, and the action behind it is the instrument M46b is built on: the City purchased the Hermann's building, 18 Mar 2024, $3.95M from the Land Sale Reserve — venue preservation by acquisition. Note for accuracy: the campaign's "at no cost to taxpayers" is not right; the Land Sale Reserve is public money. Absent: designated cultural-venue list, right-of-first-refusal, permissive tax exemption, lease-bridge fund, Old Town design code, street furniture standard.

cells.quote: Create 'complete communities' with new plazas, linear parks, and mixed-use neighbourhoods--bring back corner stores!
cells.why: Commits, and the campaign records the delivered instrument: "Pedestrianized lower Government Street and advanced other car-free spaces" plus a new pedestrian zone at Turner Plaza. Absent: Bastion Square, Fan Tan Alley, published success criteria and the reversibility rule, and any signature-project shortlist or referendum. FLAG: Government Street pedestrianisation originates in June 2020, before his October 2022 election, and no source names him in a vote — the campaign claim is his, the authorship is not established.

cells.quote: Complete the Lochside Trail & Goose widening and lighting project.
cells.why: Commits + comparable: gap-closing and lighting on the corridor that carries M47's Selkirk Trestle and Gorge Waterway links, plus "Continue to invest in parks across the city, including adding a new splash pad for kids" and "Expand green spaces and playgrounds." Absent: heritage restoration incentive fund, demolition-by-neglect rule, heritage lighting to midnight, restored Parks horticulture budget, Beacon Hill 5-year plan, per-neighbourhood signature feature.

cells.what: culture, sport, and the arts funding floor
cells.quote: Support the Our DWTN program to invest in local arts and culture
cells.why: (campaign records $1m/year), with the Festival Investment Grant, the Cultural Infrastructure Grant, Symphony Splash as an annual event and "Support upgrades to Ship Point and Royal Athletic Park for arts uses." Commits + comparable: sustained named grant programmes and year-round activation. Absent, and this is the measure's point: no published funding floor, no per-capita figure, no share-of-operating figure, no supermajority protection, no three-year operating agreements, no 6am–10pm facility standard, no restored Royal Athletic Park enhancement budget.

cells.quote: Undertake increased departmental and program reviews within city operations to increase efficiency.
cells.why: Commits, no instrument: no published three-part test, no $50K grant line, no rotation of 3–4 service areas per cycle, no published assessment or reasons, no appeal, no savings number. An intention to review is not the measure. No such review was run in four years — absence is Record, not Opposed.

cells.what: local-tech procurement, open data, Wi-Fi, EV charging
cells.quote: Make it easier to charge EVs by adding Level 2 and Level 3 EV chargers across the city and better enabling home EV charging.
cells.why: Commits + same instrument on M57, which is one of four in the cluster. Absent: local-preference procurement scoring, innovation pilot contracts, data sovereignty, open data portal expansion, air-quality sensors, public Wi-Fi.

cells.quote: Advance a decarbonization strategy and green retrofits for existing buildings, which account for 52% of Victoria's GHG emissions.
cells.why: Commits + same instrument on M58's delivery-and-publish ask; the campaign publishes a progress number against the adopted targets ("31% reduction of GHG emissions in the City since 2007, keeping Victoria on track for 2030 and 2050 goals") and records the Zero Carbon Step Code and a Climate Leadership Plan update. The 31% is a city-wide claim, not his instrument, and is not stamped as an ACTW figure. Absent: district-energy feasibility study (M58b) and the entire seismic file (M64b) — no inventory, no unreinforced-masonry work, no coastal mapping.

cells.what: trees, mode share, ecosystems, emergency preparedness
cells.quote: Increase number of trees in the city and expand urban forest canopy from current 30% to 40%.
cells.why: Commits + same instrument on M61: a published canopy target, above the Program's 35% by 2035, with 26%→30% and 150,000 trees claimed for the term. Absent: a planting number (no 5,000-tree equivalent), the 60% mode-share target (M62), the 2.7 ha/1,000 parkland and 36% natural-state constraints (M63), stormwater renewal (M59), and published Climate Friendly Homes uptake (M60). "Build walkable, cyclable, dense urban fabric" is a Mention of mode shift with no target.

cells.quote: Oversaw successful referendum to replace the Crystal Pool
cells.why: — a $168.9M new capital project taken to assent voting, 58.71% yes, 8 Feb 2025. The instrument M77 names, used once because the borrowing statute required it. No 2026 promise on a threshold, a 5-step process or a material-change rule, and nothing contradicted — shown, not scored. Context: he voted against the 23 Jan 2025 Hammond/Gardiner motion seeking balanced City information ahead of that vote.

cells.quote: Monitor and update the Council's Code of Conduct.
cells.why: Commits toward the integrity goal, and the campaign records "Implemented City's first-ever Code of Conduct policy" (Bylaw 23-058, adopted 26 Oct 2023). Not the instrument: no Integrity Commissioner, no arm's-length office, no MNP implementation tracker, no annual public report, no 60-day consultation-response standard. A code without an arm's-length commissioner is the gap M79b exists to close.

cells.quote: Actions over words, and the cap fires.
cells.why: Campaign claim: "Deferred salary adjustments to next term, following third-party impartial review process" — M79f's instrument, and it did happen (4 Apr 2024 pause and independent task force; 1 Aug 2024 approval deferred to the 2026–2030 term at 45% of the mayor's salary). The sourced miss: on 14 Mar 2024 he voted for and argued for a ~25% councillor raise effective May 2024, mid-term — "Either this is a part-time job with part-time pay and benefits, or it is a full-time job with full-time pay and benefits." The deferral followed the backlash, not the principle. Incumbent cap holds this below Close. Absent: lobbyist registry, FOI fee abolition, mandate letters, portfolio scorecards.

cells.what: neighbourhoods, language access, Local Area Plans
community surveys, turnout and ballot access
Saanich amalgamation (one line, not the whole topic)
cells.quote: Voted NO 25 Jun 2026, 5–4, on the non-binding ballot question, with Hammond, Gardiner and Thompson — and moved a defeated amendment to send the question back to the Province for additional financial and transitional analysis, which is M81's own instrument.
cells.why: "I did not sign up for a temperature check. I'd rather cut out the fat and go right to the binding question as soon as possible." He called it "a proper mess." The word Saanich does not appear on the 2026 site, so there is no promise to contradict — shown, not scored. FLAG: this is the card's biggest single swing. If a June 2026 council action in the election year counts as 2026 text, this becomes Aligned 3.0, n = 31, and the internal proposal moves from C to B.
